findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in the reports bucket (including the seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with SSE-KMS or a managed key.

No acl or public access block is specified and no bucket policy is visible, so the bucket relies entirely on account defaults for access control; combined with the absence of a public access block this risks unintended public or cross-account exposure.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this bucket and its objects is not recorded, hampering detection and forensic investigation of data exposure.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version, allowing silent tampering or destruction of archived reports.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest by configuration.
No logging block is defined for this bucket, so access to ledger exports is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of ledger export objects is unrecoverable.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored model artifacts are not encrypted at rest by explicit configuration.

No server_side_encryption_configuration is set on the runbooks bucket; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedural and credential-adjacent information and should be encrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to the runbooks bucket is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL; it appears to be a corrupted form of "log-delivery-write". An invalid or unintended ACL on the audit trail bucket risks either apply failure or an access-control state that does not match intent for a log-delivery target.

force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows the entire log store, including logs written by model_artifacts, to be deleted along with its contents on a terraform destroy, undermining audit-log integrity.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/contact data) is uploaded without a server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that itself has no default encryption configured, so it is stored in cleartext.
